pr_summary: Ensure the bpfman RPC server creates socket directories at startup and initializes logging properly. The RPC binary must create /run/bpfman-sock (and optionally /run/bpfman/csi for CSI support) before binding the socket, and both RPC and CLI binaries must initialize logging (journald if under systemd, otherwise env_logger) with RUST_LOG environment variable support.
patch_file_cues: RUST_LOG environment variable for log level configuration
create_dir_all - directory creation for socket paths
test_file_cues: cargo xtask integration-test - integration test runner
platform_constraint_evidence: Cargo.toml workspace.metadata.vendor-filter platforms only list Linux targets (aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, i686-unknown-linux-gnu, powerpc64le-unknown-linux-gnu, s390x-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
Dependencies include libsystemd and systemd-journal-logger (Linux systemd specific)
Socket paths use Unix domain sockets (/run/bpfman-sock)
Dependencies include libbpf, nix crate with unix features
notes: This is a Rust project (bpfman) that manages eBPF programs. The fix involves ensuring socket directories are created at startup and logging is properly initialized. The project is Linux-only due to systemd dependencies, eBPF requirements, and Unix domain socket usage. No test.patch file exists - tests may need to be synthesized. Key build tool is 'cargo xtask' for custom build tasks. The project requires libbpf and other system dependencies for eBPF functionality.
